canonical_source.resolved_control: Cancel button shown while Site Details synchronization is running
canonical_source.behavior: The source invokes CancellationTokenSource.Cancel() for the currently running WordPress synchronization and handles OperationCanceledException as user-requested cancellation.

laravel_adaptation.adaptation_reason: Laravel synchronization is queue-backed rather than held by a page-local CancellationTokenSource, so the canonical cancel intent is preserved as a tenant-authorized cooperative cancel request consumed by the existing real Sync runtime.

tenant_isolation.proof: Focused acceptance rejects a content.edit user attempting to cancel a foreign-tenant Site ID and rejects a caller without content.edit before mutation.
tenant_isolation.caller_override_probe: Cancellation resolves the active run only from the tenant-scoped Site ID and never accepts tenant ownership or sync-run ownership metadata from the request body.

semantics.external_dependency: No external provider success is required or claimed by cancellation itself.
semantics.no_active_behavior: HTTP 409; no run or SyncCancelled event is fabricated
semantics.race_behavior: stale run, batch and item writes cannot restore progress or completion after cancellation has been requested

coverage: exact canonical operation identity and source metadata
authenticated tenant-context active and cancel route bindings
409 and no fabricated event when no sync is active
stale runtime model cannot resurrect cancellation
canonical operation ID submitted to cancellation endpoint
accepted cancellation request reflected without fabricated sync completion

terminality.basis: The canonical user cancellation is implemented against the existing Laravel Sync runtime with operation-linked production and focused-test markers, tenant/permission enforcement, cooperative queue cancellation, explicit no-active failure semantics, and race guards preventing stale completion after cancellation.
